Stated Claim / Post Context:
In calling for an end to the Iran War, Vance walks a fine line with Trump

A rift is opening up between President Trump and Vice President Vance when it comes to the Iran War. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Susan Glasser, staff writer at the New Yorker.

Actual Article Body:
Ayesha Rascoe

A rift is opening up between President Trump and Vice President Vance when it comes to the Iran War. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Susan Glasser, staff writer at the New Yorker.

AYESHA RASCOE, HOST:  The day after Republicans suffered a major defeat in the midterm elections, Vice President JD Vance posted a list of what Republicans could do to win back disillusioned voters. No. 1 - end the war in Iran. President Trump said he didn't disagree. But last week he posted, quote, "we don't need a deal with Iran." Instead of focusing on Iran, Trump said he was asking Vance to turn his complete and total attention to corruption and crime in cities and states run by Democrats.Joining us now is Susan Glasser, staff writer at The New Yorker. Thank you so much for joining us.SUSAN GLASSER: Oh, great to be with you.RASCOE: Did you read President Trump's post as a response to Vance's criticism of the war?GLASSER: I mean, not to be too blunt, but basically, you have the president of the United States saying to his own vice president, yeah. You're kind of fired from the most important issue that we have, which is how to resolve this unresolved and unwon conflict in the Middle East. If anything, because of how overwhelming the scale of the Democratic victory was in the elections, we've kind of understated the extent to which it is a remarkable thing to have had Vice President Vance publicly blame the president's top foreign policy priority for that overwhelming defeat. Of course, we know Donald Trump. He's furious about this.RASCOE: When Vance said the war is the problem, one thing that stood out to me is he kind of was talking about it as if he wasn't in the administration. Like, he didn't put himself in it.GLASSER: No. I think the big-picture context here, Ayesha, is clearly that Vice President Vance feels his chances, such as they are, for becoming president after Trump slipping away, largely due to the war. Donald Trump, of course, campaigned in 2024 saying he was the candidate of no new wars. And Vance was specifically selected from what you might call the real MAGA America First wing of the Republican Party.For him, this is even more foundational. His people have gone to great lengths, it seems to me, to put out in news reports that he was against the war from the beginning in the private councils that the president had, even though it has technically been his portfolio since the spring to negotiate an end to the conflict with Iran. Obviously, that...
